root_idea.summary: The root centers on clarity that enables perception: seeing with the eyes, understanding with the mind, and the evidence or insight that makes a matter clear.
root_idea.development: One semantic branch develops from perceptive clarity into sight, knowledge, insight, proof, and manifestness. A second branch concerns thickness or joined edges, yielding terms for sewn hides, cloth seams, stones, and related material forms.

senses.definition: To see or become seeing; to perceive with the eyes.
senses.usage_conditions: Form I can describe the acquisition or exercise of sight. In Quranic use, the physical act of watching can carry an accompanying sense of awareness.

senses.definition: To perceive mentally; to know or understand.
senses.usage_conditions: Commonly construed with بِـ; the Quranic expression بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا بِهِ contrasts the speaker’s understanding with what others did not perceive.

senses.definition: To cause someone to perceive or recognize; to make aware.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic passive construction يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ, persons are made to perceive or recognize one another, including by recognizing their identifying features or consequences.

senses.definition: To see; to look at or behold.
senses.usage_conditions: The ordinary Form IV verb of visual perception; it may take the person or thing seen as its object, or occur with a directional construction meaning to look toward someone.
The form may extend from visual perception to apprehension and understanding, especially when the object is a matter rather than a visible thing.

senses.definition: How clearly one sees; to see clearly, in an emphatic exclamatory construction.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic أَبْصِرْ بِهِ and أَسْمِعْ بِهِ constructions are idiomatic expressions of the clarity or completeness of seeing and hearing, not ordinary imperatives.

senses.definition: Sight, eyesight, or the eye as the organ of seeing.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural أَبْصَار commonly denotes eyes, sight, or visual faculties; the singular can refer to the eye or to its power of perception.
The noun can denote the heart’s or mind’s perceptive faculty, especially where bodily sight is contrasted with understanding or insight.
As a human description it means seeing or clear-sighted; as a divine epithet it denotes complete sight of apparent and hidden things without a bodily organ.

senses.definition: Insight, mental perception, knowledge, or assured understanding.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic phrase عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ expresses action grounded in knowledge and certainty; بَصَائِر can denote sources or forms of insight.

senses.definition: An evidence, proof, or admonitory example that makes a matter clear.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural بَصَائِر is used for revealed signs or lessons serving as evidence and warning.

senses.definition: A witness or observing faculty that testifies concerning a person.
senses.usage_conditions: In بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ, the expression is interpreted as the person or bodily members being witnesses for or against him.
The active participle can describe people who see or perceive.

senses.definition: Causing visibility; giving light or making perception possible.
senses.usage_conditions: When applied to the day or a natural phenomenon, it can mean that it enables seeing, gives light, or renders things perceptible.

senses.definition: Illuminating or causing sight; making something perceptible.
senses.usage_conditions: The feminine active participle can describe a sign or phenomenon that enables people to see or perceive.
The form may describe a sign whose conspicuousness makes its reality clear; this is a resultative sense rather than a new physical act of seeing.

senses.definition: Seeking or possessing clear mental perception; discerning.
senses.usage_conditions: The Form X participle can emphasize seeking insight or being endowed with it. In the Quranic passage it is explained both as having perceptive knowledge and as recognizing the likely consequence of one’s actions.

senses.definition: The giving of insight; clarification or instruction that makes something understood.
senses.usage_conditions: As the verbal noun of بَصَّرَ, it denotes making perceptible or intelligible, including instruction that brings understanding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To join two hides or their edges by placing one over the other and sewing them together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A material and technical use concerning the particular method of joining hides or cloth edges.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To open the eyes of a young animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative physical use, especially said of a whelp whose eyes have opened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to see, perceive, know, or understand; to acquaint someone with something or make it apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader causative range includes physical sight, knowledge, understanding, and the rendering of a matter manifest; the Quran-specific interpersonal passive use is listed under the Quranic Form II entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To smear arrow feathers with blood or strengthen and fasten them with glue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use concerning the preparation of arrows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go or come to the city of al-Baṣrah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-name use of the Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look at something while competing with another to see it first; to look at one another in such competition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or competitive looking construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rise above surrounding objects in order to look toward someone or something from afar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized posture-and-distance use of the Form III verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To abandon unbelief and adopt true belief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative use in which seeing signifies entering into sound belief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hang a بصيرة, an oblong piece of cloth, on the door of a dwelling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional household use associated with the noun بَصِيرَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look closely, examine, or study something repeatedly in order to gain clear knowledge of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form V verb can also mean to consider what may happen, seeking to discover its consequences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To see one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pretend to see, either physically or mentally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the opposite of feigning blindness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a road to become plain, clear, manifest, or conspicuous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form X use applied to a road or route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thickness of a thing, such as a heaven, earth, skin, garment, or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A material noun distinct from the perception branch of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The side or edge of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a related transposed form of the material sense of thickness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cotton.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A material noun linked in the lexical discussion to the cloth sense of بَصِيرَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the sunset prayer, and according to another usage for the dawn prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the time when darkness is mixed with light and visible forms or stars can be seen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The time or circumstance in which objects can still be distinguished at the onset of darkness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in the adverbial expression لَقِيَهُ بَصَرًا, describing meeting when there remained enough light for recognition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vacant tract of land in the idiom describing a place where nothing but the earth hears or sees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression rather than a general meaning of ordinary sight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft, whitish, glistening, rugged, or gypsum-bearing stones; by extension, rugged gypsum-like ground or tough clay containing pebbles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact shade and hardness vary across the reported lexical explanations, but the use denotes a stony or gypsum-bearing material or terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good red land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or specialized land description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land containing stones sharp enough to cut the hooves of animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjective for difficult stony ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dog.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transferred naming based on the dog’s sharp sight; this is not the ordinary adjective meaning “seeing.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Endowed with mental perception, knowledge, understanding, intelligence, or skill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Typically construed with بِـ, as in being knowledgeable or skilled in a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet for a blind or weak-sighted person, or a believer, by reversal or auspicious usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an established ironic or benevolent application and does not mean that the person has ordinary physical sight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Belief or firm belief of the heart; certainty and assurance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also occurs in expressions meaning according to knowledge and assurance, or intentionally; these extensions are broader than the specific Quranic insight sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Constancy or firmness in religion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized religious extension of assured inner perception.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A glistening portion or patch of blood, especially blood on the ground by which a wounded animal is tracked; also blood-revenge or a homicide fine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word covers several reported specifications of the amount, shape, flow, or location of the blood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shield, coat of mail, or defensive armor; plural بَصَائِر can denote worn arms.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete material meaning distinct from the Quranic plural meaning “insights” or “proofs.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oblong piece or strip of cotton or other cloth, including a cloth hung at a dwelling’s door.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can also denote a cloth panel or piece used in a joined garment or tent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The joined and sewn portion between two oblong cloth pieces, such as in a tent or waterskin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical textile sense related to the verb بَصَرَ “to sew joined edges.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intent or forceful glance; by extension, something manifest, severe, or terrifying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the conventional expression لَمْحٌ بَاصِرٌ and related figurative descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Visible food in the proverb contrasting early morning meals with evening meals seen before nightfall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proverb-specific plural usage derived from the notion of visibility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sharper-sighted or clearer-sighted; more perceptive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or elative adjective, not the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A watcher or guard set in a garden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative agent-noun use of the active participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion that sees prey from afar and pursues it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative animal epithet based on keen sight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who hangs a بصيرة cloth at the door of a dwelling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional agent-noun use associated with the cloth sense of بَصِيرَة.

cautions: بَصَر and بَصِيرَة can denote either bodily sight or inner perception; the relevant construction and context determine the branch.
The classical epithet بَصِير for a blind person is an ironic or auspicious usage and should not be confused with the ordinary meaning “seeing.”
Lane’s Quran references use historical citation conventions; the modern verse locations in the examples are taken only from the supplied QAC occurrence data.
The Quranic Form II occurrence is passive and has an interpersonal construction; it should not be reduced to the ordinary active causative gloss without that constructional nuance.
